text: Fill in the missing agent or term for each class of mitochondrial disruption.
questions: The insecticide *rotenone:A plant-derived insecticide also used in Parkinson's disease research.* inhibits Complex I by blocking electron transfer from iron-sulphur clusters to coenzyme Q.

In *cyanide:Seen in electroplating workers, fire-smoke inhalation and cassava ingestion.* poisoning, the toxin binds to haem a3 of Complex IV, so venous blood stays bright red because oxygen cannot accept electrons.
Lipid-soluble weak acids called *uncouplers:2,4-dinitrophenol is the classic pharmacological example.* carry protons back into the matrix, raising oxygen consumption while stopping ATP synthesis.
Neonates maintain body temperature using *thermogenin/UCP1:Also called uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1).* in brown adipose tissue, which diverts the proton gradient into heat.

Muscle biopsies in mitochondrial diseases characteristically show *ragged-red:Seen with Gomori trichrome stain; indicates compensatory mitochondrial proliferation.* fibres from proliferating abnormal mitochondria beneath the sarcolemma.

overallFeedback.feedback: Each class of mitochondrial disruption affects oxygen consumption differently: chain inhibitors stop both electron flow and O2 use; uncouplers raise O2 use but abolish ATP synthesis; and ATP synthase blockers slow both by building an unopposed gradient. Recognising the agent from the clinical pattern is essential for emergency management.
